title: Nozomi AI assistant — agent that acts across apps, from Cursor to Kalshi
summary: A 19-year-old YC S25 founder's personal assistant demo that takes real actions across tools, coding in Cursor and placing Kalshi bets. The viral hook is a creepy social-monitoring feature that tracks Instagram accounts for breakup signals. Mostly hype and ethics bait, little technical detail.
takeaways: Agent assistants that act across consumer apps are now YC-fundable demos
Social-signal monitoring is trivially easy for agents, which is a privacy red flag

title: Princeton sponsored-ads study — 18 of 23 AI assistants push the paid option
summary: Carousel on a Princeton study that gave 23 models a sponsored option and a cheaper better one across flights, loans and shopping. 18 of 23 favored the sponsored pick, GPT-5.1 surfaced it 94% of the time, and a 'serve the customer only' system prompt barely moved it. Note the creator's caveat: it measures susceptibility in a hypothetical deployment, not real paid placement.
takeaways: Treat AI shopping or booking recommendations as potentially ad-biased
System-prompt instructions to ignore the company did not fix the bias in GPT-5.1
The study tests a hypothetical sponsorship setup, not live ad behavior

title: Vibe-coded website showcase — list of standout AI-built sites
summary: A Manus-sponsored post promising a list of impressive websites (Bklit.com among them) behind a comment gate. No list content is in the captured post. Attached OCR appears to belong to a different post about ADHD-style Claude prompts.
takeaways: Paid partnership with Manus, treat as promo
Bklit.com is one of the featured sites

title: Artist statement — a four-sentence formula that cuts the art-speak
summary: A plain template for artist statements: what you make, why this and nothing else, how you make it (only the meaningful part), and what you want viewers to take away. Ends with a pitch for the creator's book VISIBLE.
takeaways: Sentence one says what you make in plain English
Sentence two names the question you keep circling
Only describe process where it carries meaning
Close with what the viewer should take away

title: Claude ambition prompt — four knobs to make AI aim higher
summary: Covers a post by Claude's lead engineer on tuning AI ambition along speed, altitude, depth and range. The appendable prompt asks Claude what a top professional would do that you didn't ask for, what raw material they'd start from, which methods and tools they'd use, and who besides you would judge the result, then rewrites the prompt to ask for exactly that.
takeaways: Append the four-question ambition prompt to any task
Ask what an expert would start from instead of predigested material
Have the model rewrite your prompt before executing it
Stop using frontier models only for one-off small tasks

title: Agent Reach — open-source skill letting agents read Reddit and X
summary: An open-source repo installed as a Claude skill that gives agents access to 13 platforms without API costs. The demo shows Claude failing to fetch a Reddit post and an X thread, then succeeding with comments once Agent Reach is installed.
takeaways: Agents' built-in fetch tools are blocked by Reddit and X
Agent Reach adds read access to 13 platforms without paid APIs
Install it by telling Claude to install the repo

title: Five fringe GitHub repos — WiFi sensing, offline 400B LLM, satellite capture
summary: A hype-framed listicle of open-source projects: RuView turns WiFi into a through-wall person sensor, Flash MoE runs a 400B model on an iPhone offline, a walk-through camera tool builds 3D replicas of buildings, an app detects nearby camera glasses, and a cheap dish plus SDR pulls live weather-satellite images. Repo links are comment-gated.
takeaways: WiFi CSI sensing can detect people through walls
Mixture-of-experts flash offloading can run huge models on phones, slowly
Weather satellite imagery is receivable with a small dish and cheap radio

title: EMA9 + VWAP crossover — automated 3-minute options strategy pitch
summary: Promo for the RoboQuant platform: buy calls or puts when EMA9 crosses VWAP on the 3-minute chart, with a claimed $179k month and 79.9% prop-challenge pass rate. The backtest claims are unverified marketing, though the crossover rule itself is a simple, testable baseline.
takeaways: The rule is EMA9 crossing VWAP on 3-minute bars, calls up and puts down
Profit and pass-rate claims are unverified promo
Worth backtesting yourself as a baseline, not trusting

title: Abliterated Qwen 3.5 9B — run PewDiePie-style Ajax locally with llama.cpp
summary: Walkthrough of running an abliterated Qwen 3.5 9B GGUF (the base of PewDiePie's Ajax model) locally: download from Hugging Face, install llama.cpp via Homebrew, start llama-server with context size and port, then point the DeepSeek harness at the custom endpoint. Also mentions PewDiePie's Odysseus agent harness.
takeaways: Abliterated models remove refusals more thoroughly than plain uncensored fine-tunes
brew install llama.cpp then llama-server -m <model> --ctx-size --port 8080
A 16-bit 9B model (~17 GB) runs on a 32 GB MacBook Pro
Any agent harness with a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint can drive it

title: REA MCP — agent-driven reverse engineering with a Ghidra backend
summary: REA is an MCP server that lets an AI agent reverse engineer apps and stripped native binaries, with Ghidra doing the decompilation while the agent drives and cites evidence per call. The creator decompiled a closed-source program in three to four minutes on Ubuntu. Setup is deferred to a follow-up video.
takeaways: Pair an agent with Ghidra over MCP to recover logic from stripped binaries
Evidence-per-call output makes agent RE findings auditable
Use only on software you are authorized to analyze

title: Claude Opus 5.5 to Blender — 3D animation built entirely as code
summary: Claude Opus 5.5 wrote everything: a web mock of the After Effects UI, a Python script that builds the Blender scene, the character animation, plus the music and sound effects. Blender rendered 360 frames on GPU in about 15 minutes and FFmpeg stitched the video. Full prompt is comment-gated.
takeaways: Have the LLM emit a Blender Python script instead of using a video model
Render frames in Blender and assemble with FFmpeg
Audio and SFX can also be generated as code

title: Mandelbulb — ray-marching a 3D fractal from z⁸ + c
summary: Explains the Mandelbulb: Daniel White's spherical-coordinate trick for 3D 'multiplication', raised to power 8 by Paul Nylander, rendered by ray marching with the distance estimate d = ½·r·log r/dr. Code is ported line by line from Mandelbulber's GPL-3.0 source, with the Hamilton 'multiply triplets' history as a bonus.
takeaways: Power-8 spherical formula: r→r⁸, θ→8θ, φ→8φ, then add c
Distance estimate d = ½·r·log r / dr lets rays jump safely
Mandelbulber2 source is a clean reference implementation

title: Claude Code vs smart TV — stripping bloatware over local WiFi
summary: Short clip on pointing Claude Code at a smart TV on the same WiFi network to remove bloatware and customize it, with before/after speed comparisons. The prompt is shown but no device specifics or method details are given.
takeaways: Claude Code can drive devices reachable on your LAN, e.g. via ADB on Android TVs
Be on the same network as the target device

title: Duss.o Labs 'Wobbles' — procedural Blender loop scored in Ableton
summary: LAB/018, an experimental procedural animation made in Blender with a self-produced Ableton soundtrack. Pure visual reference, no process breakdown.
takeaways: Reference for soft-body style procedural motion synced to music
Low-signal save, keep only as a trend marker

title: ChatGPT Astra 6 — comment-gated SEO ranking link
summary: Engagement bait praising ChatGPT Astra 6 for SEO with a comment-to-get-link hook. The transcript has no content.
takeaways: No usable content, only a gated link
Low-signal save, keep only as a trend marker

title: CoreWeave debt explained — how GPU-backed loans fund the neoclouds
summary: An ex-Morgan Stanley CDO structurer explains the neocloud stack (landlords, vertically integrated players like IREN and Crusoe, CoreWeave, Nebius) and why CoreWeave's GPU-backed asset financing spooked markets. Advance rates hit 90-95% against off-taker credit, and loan, contract and GPU useful life are nearly the same length, leaving a thin tail.
takeaways: Neoclouds can borrow 90-95% of capex against strong off-takers like Meta
GPU loans have a short tail because asset life barely exceeds the contract
Post-contract hourly GPU rental is the bull case for the debt

title: Block Blast reverse-engineered — on-device XGBoost rigs difficulty for ad revenue
summary: A reverse engineer found Block Blast runs a local XGBoost model on device signals (phone model, country, past ad revenue, vibration setting) to predict your ad value and adjust difficulty. Rules like 'Boost Then Kill' and 'High Value Ad Harvest' trigger a 'death algorithm' right when a pricey revive ad is ready. Full code evidence is promised later on the creator's site.
takeaways: Free-to-play difficulty can be tuned per player to ad value
On-device ML models are discoverable by decompiling the app
Revive-ad timing is A/B tested to the minute

title: Claudex skill — Claude and GPT-6 Astra cross-audit plan and build
summary: A free skill that splits work between two frontier models: Claude writes the plan and GPT-6 Astra audits it until it holds, then roles swap so Astra builds and Claude audits. Runs inside Claude or Codex as a reusable skill.
takeaways: Do not let one model plan, build and grade its own work
Swap planner and auditor roles between build phases
Package the loop as a skill so it is reusable

title: Headless software + MCP — Chamath on why software IP stops being a moat
summary: Breaks down Chamath's All-In claim that software IP is worthless once services go headless and agents call them via MCP. With Salesforce and xAI's Grok exposing headless engines, agents pick tools on speed, cost or accuracy, so the interface stops being the moat.
takeaways: Design products to be driven by agents, not just humans
MCP is the plug that lets agents switch between tools
The interface is no longer a defensible moat

title: Qwen 27B at home — a dev ditching frontier labs for local models
summary: An ex-lab engineer argues the free Qwen 27B model, run locally or in the cloud, handles long complex tasks better than frontier labs. Also claims Blackwell chips, including their Jetson Thor boxes, have broken speculative decoding. Opinion-heavy with strong unverified claims.
takeaways: Open-weight Qwen models are viable for long agentic tasks
Speculative decoding issues on new Blackwell hardware may hurt LLM speed
Treat the anti-lab claims as opinion

title: Reverse Engineer Anything — trending repo that explains how any app works
summary: The week's top trending GitHub repo, about 70k stars: point Claude Code or Codex at an app and it explains how the feature is built so you can rebuild it. Users have revived old hardware, e.g. a Logitech keypad on Linux in 15 minutes, plus scanners and sound cards that lost drivers.
takeaways: Use agents to study how a favorite feature is implemented
Revive unsupported hardware by reverse engineering its protocol
Runs locally, free

title: Game decompilation with AI — which reconstruction methods stay legal
summary: Covers five decompilation approaches (matching decompilation, functional reconstruction, static recompilation, engine re-implementation, porting recovered source) and argues engine re-implementation and functional reconstruction are the legal paths. AI fits because the original game's GPU pixel output is a verifiable oracle for rewriting the engine in a new language.
takeaways: Clean re-implementation that matches behavior is the defensible route
Comparing rendered pixel output gives the agent an automatic test oracle
Avoid shipping recovered original source

title: Tencent WorldClaw — prompt-to-3D worlds with every object a separate asset
summary: Tencent's WorldClaw generates a whole 3D scene from a prompt where every tree, house and lamp post is an editable mesh. It chains image generation (GPT Image 2), Segment Anything to split objects, and Hunyuan 2D-to-3D, with depth, normal and instance maps. Not publicly available yet.
takeaways: Pipeline pattern: generate image, segment objects, lift each to 3D
Useful for game environments and robot sim training
Not yet usable, watch for release
